title: A proof run is only at one full commit whose tree has no uncommitted change
when: RecordProofRun runs with a clean tree at the full commit, and then with a short commit, a branch, an upper-case commit, a tree at another commit, a changed file and an untracked file. Then ReadCheckout reads git repositories in which git status, as the repository and the user configure it, shows no change: a clean one, and ones with a change hidden by skip-worktree, a spec change hidden by assume-unchanged, an untracked file hidden by info/exclude, an untracked file hidden by the user's excludes file, another commit's tree shown by a replace ref, a same-size change hidden by minimal stat checks, and a new file hidden by an untracked .gitignore that ignores itself. ReadCommittedSpec reads the spec at the commit of the repositories whose spec change is hidden or replaced.
then: The clean runs give a proof run at the commit. atOneCleanCommit refuses each other run, and the store gets nothing. The spec read at the commit does not hold the hidden or replaced test record.

title: Every automated test record has an outcome, and a test that did not run is failed with did not run
when: With a spec of three automated test records and one that is not automated yet: RecordProofRun reads output in which only one automated test ran, and it was skipped.
then: The proof run holds the three automated test records in ID order: the skipped one as skipped, and the two others as failed with the detail did not run. The record that is not automated yet has no outcome.

title: A proof run with an outcome for an unknown ID is refused and names each such ID
when: RecordProofRun reads output with two IDs that are not test records, and then output with the ID of a test record that is not automated yet.
then: outcomesNameKnownRecords refuses the first run and names both IDs in order, and the store gets nothing. The second run is accepted with that outcome.

title: A proof run is attested only by the provider's trusted signer with its commit as subject
when: RecordProofRun runs in the trusted workflow at main, and then in another workflow. attestedByTrustedSigner checks the trusted workflow at main, and attestations with another commit, predicate type, workflow, repository or issuer.
then: The proof run's attestation names the commit, the proof run predicate type and the trusted signer, and the trusted workflow at main is accepted. Each other attestation is refused, and the run in another workflow is refused with nothing given to the store.

title: A proof run is never written as a file in the product's repository
when: GitHubAttestations hands over a proof run to a file at the repository's root, in a folder of the repository, through a path that climbs back in, through a link to a folder or a file in the repository, and through a relative path from inside it.
then: outsideTheRepository refuses each, and the repository keeps its files as they were. A file in a folder outside the repository is accepted.

title: A test record gets one outcome: failed if any run failed, else skipped if any was skipped, else passed
when: RecordProofRun reads Go and Python output in which each test record ID runs two or three times: passed, failed and passed; passed, skipped and passed; skipped and failed; passed twice.
then: Each test record has one outcome: failed, skipped, failed and passed.

title: A change decision names the change's commit, the base head and both coverages, and a release decision names only its commit
when: namesBothCommits checks a change decision with both commits and both coverages and a release decision with only its commit; then change decisions with no base head, a short one, a branch, no base coverage or a short commit, release decisions with a base head or a base coverage, and a decision of no gate kind.
then: The first two are accepted, and the change decision's text names both commits and both coverages. Each other decision is refused by namesBothCommits.

title: A refused decision names every obligation that fell and every test record that did not pass, and a passed decision names no reason
when: namesEveryCause checks, against two obligations that fell and two test records that did not pass, a refusal that names all four and a passed decision with no reason; then a refusal that leaves out an obligation, one that leaves out a test record, a refusal with no reason, and a passed decision with reasons.
then: The first two are accepted, and the refusal's text lists each cause on a line of its own. Each other decision is refused by namesEveryCause, which names the cause left out.

title: A passed release decision is handed to the attestation action about its commit, for the trusted signer at main, and nothing else is
when: With a fixture repository whose release commit is fully proved and a passed proof run signed at main: assure gate release runs as the gate-release job of the trusted workflow at main; then as a job of the trusted workflow at a pull request's ref and as a job of another workflow; then with a failed test; then with a predicate file inside the repository, and with a step summary inside the repository; then, for a passed and for a refused release, with an earlier file already at the predicate's path; then, with a step summary file set, at a commit whose spec has a test record of an invariant that does not exist, and for the passed release with the predicate's folder read-only. Then it runs with a step summary file set and no --predicate. Reads the attest-release job of proof-run.yml and runs its subject step for the commit.
then: The first run passes, its decision names the attestation at the release-decision predicate type about the commit, for the proof-run workflow at main, and it writes a predicate that is a passed release decision about the commit. releaseAttested refuses the passed decision in the two other jobs: each exits 2 with no decision and writes no predicate. The refused decision names no attestation and writes no predicate. With the predicate or the step summary inside the repository, and with an earlier file at the predicate's path, the gate exits 2 before it decides, prints no decision, writes no predicate and leaves the earlier file as it was; the repository has no change. At the commit with the broken spec the gate exits 2 and the step summary holds only one line that says no decision was reached. With the read-only folder the gate exits 2, writes no predicate, and the step summary holds the passed decision and then one line that says no decision was reached because the predicate is not written; this part is not checked when the tests run as root. With no --predicate it exits 2, and the step summary holds one line that says no decision was reached because the gate is called wrongly. The attest-release job is exactly its allowed keys and steps, and signs the predicate at the release-decision predicate type, with the commit as the subject that its subject step names.

title: The same causes give the same reasons in the same fixed order, and reasons out of that order are refused
when: The causes of a refusal, obligations that fell from shares, are absent at the change or lack a share at a release commit, no verified proof run, test records not passed, code-standard faults and workflow files that differ, are given in three orders, one with causes twice, and each gives a decision; then reasonsInFixedOrder checks reasons with a test record before an obligation, a workflow file before a test record, built before designed, obligations out of order, an absent obligation before another, proved before built at a release, a share not had before an obligation, the missing proof run after a test record, test records or workflow files out of order, a code fault before a test record, before an obligation or before the missing proof run, a workflow file before a code fault, code faults out of rule order or of one rule out of key order, and a reason or a code fault twice.
then: Each order gives the same reasons in the fixed order, each once: obligations, the proof run and test records, code faults by rule and key, then workflow files; and the same decision text, byte for byte. Each list out of the fixed order is refused by reasonsInFixedOrder.

title: A failed or interrupted resolution leaves go.mod and go.sum as they were, or recoverable to the resolved pair
when: With a project with applied code, go.mod and go.sum, and a fake go runner: Resolution fails in nine ways (the tidy, verify, list and diff commands; a source file added, edited or deleted during the run; go.mod edited during the run; and cancellation), and is interrupted at four points of the apply journal (before it is written, when it is written, after its first operation, and before it is complete).
then: Each failed run keeps the bytes of go.mod and go.sum and leaves no journal. An interruption before the journal is written keeps the old pair; each later interruption asks for recovery, and recovery writes exactly the resolved pair and removes the journal.

title: A saved overlay flag and ambient GOFLAGS cannot change what resolution reads
when: With a project with applied code, a Go configuration file that saves a -overlay flag naming another import, an invalid ambient GOFLAGS, and the local Go SDK offline: Resolution runs.
then: The overlay's import never reaches go.mod, and the source is unchanged.
notes: It covers the example the invariant names, a saved -overlay flag, plus ambient GOFLAGS and a GOWORK that points nowhere (ST-BLD-UC01-R02-T02). A real go.work or -modfile is not exercised.

title: A cache holds only module zips whose hashes go.sum states, and its record lists each
when: With a download cache of two module zips, one with an escaped path, and the hashes go.sum states for them: the cache is checked; then go.sum loses one hash; then it states a different hash for one zip; and cache records with no modules, a bad hash, a wrong order, a repeated module or an invalid path are checked.
then: The first check lists both modules by path, version and hash in order, and the record that lists them is valid. The zip that go.sum does not state is refused by name, the zip whose hash differs is refused with both hashes, and each changed record is refused.

title: A build runs with the proxy off from its recorded cache, and fails when a module is missing or differs
when: With a real build from a downloaded module cache: its record is read; then builds run from copies of the cache in which the module zip is missing, and in which it is changed.
then: The record names the module proxy off and the cache's inventory, and its environment sets GOPROXY off. Each build from a broken copy fails.
notes: It runs on the real build in TestBuildIsReproducibleAndRecordsEveryInput, so it needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass.

title: A build refuses an SDK that is not the verified one
when: With build options naming a fake go binary: Build runs.
then: It refuses the SDK and writes no work directory.
notes: Not proof yet: the pin is the compiler's sdkIdentity constant, not the archetype's; the archetype pin is not built (ST-SUP-INV08). Accepting the right SDK needs the real SDK.

title: Two builds from the same inputs give byte-identical executables, records and SBOMs
when: With a committed project, its downloaded module cache and the pinned Go SDK: stego build runs twice into new folders, each build building twice inside.
then: The two results hold byte-identical executables, build records, SPDX SBOMs and CycloneDX SBOMs.
notes: It runs on the real build in TestBuildIsReproducibleAndRecordsEveryInput, so it needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass.

title: The record of a real build names every input and the fixed build settings, and no credential
when: With a committed project that the compiler applied, whose generated program needs one small module, its downloaded module cache, the pinned Go SDK, and a credential and GOFLAGS in the caller's environment: stego build runs from the cache.
then: build.json names the revision, the Go SDK, the module cache inventory, the generation record, both builds, the executable's digest and the digest of every committed file; it sets CGO off, no workspace, the local toolchain, no GOFLAGS, the proxy off, telemetry off, read-only modules, trimmed paths, no PGO and no source stamping; it holds neither the credential, the caller's GOFLAGS, PATH nor HOME.
notes: It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass. It builds a small program twice in each of two builds, about a minute.

title: An image build refuses an untrusted build record, CA bundle or executable and never reads the host's trust store
when: With a build record, its executable and an explicit CA bundle on disk, and SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR set to another CA: BuildImage runs with an untrusted build record digest, an untrusted CA digest, the host's CA bundle, a leaf certificate bundle, no CA bundle, an executable the record does not name, and an executable that is not the built one; then an image is assembled from the explicit CA bundle.
then: Each build is refused and writes no image.json; the assembled image holds the explicit CA bundle only, and an empty, private key or leaf certificate bundle is refused.
notes: TestTrustStoreRejectsKeysAndNonCACertificates in the same file also carries this ID and covers each malformed CA bundle. The accepted build needs a real Go executable that Verify accepts, so the success path is shown through assembleImage.

title: An image signature holds both SBOMs of its build record as signed attestations
when: With an image folder as image build writes it, with both SBOMs, and a provider verifier that gives an SPDX and a CycloneDX attestation about the image digest by the trusted signer: SignImage runs; then with the CycloneDX attestation of another predicate type, the SPDX attestation twice, a changed SPDX predicate, a changed CycloneDX file, an unsigned CycloneDX bundle, and a removed SPDX file.
then: The first run writes signature.json with both attestations in the order SPDX, CycloneDX and the digest of each SBOM, and a second run does not replace it; each change is refused and writes no signature.json.

title: A signature by any identity other than the pipeline's trusted signer is refused
when: With a trusted keyless signer: the signer check runs on another workflow, another reference, another issuer, a key and keyless identity, no identity, a key, and a subject with no exact reference; on trusted signers that are both, neither, without an exact reference, on plain HTTP or with a short key digest; and SignImage runs on an image whose SBOM attestations are by another workflow.
then: Each other identity and each invalid trusted signer is refused, and SignImage refuses the image, names the trusted signer and writes no signature.json.
notes: Which signer a provider has comes from the service's delivery pipeline (ST-DLV-INV04); here the trusted signer is an input of the test.

title: The same build gives the same image, running as non-root
when: With one executable and one CA bundle: The image is assembled twice, in two different directories.
then: Both records are equal and both OCI layouts have the same digests; the config runs as user 65532, with entrypoint /service and SSL_CERT_FILE set.
notes: It calls assembleImage, the whole of what stego image build writes after its checks.

title: The source snapshot is the Git tree of the revision
when: With a revision whose export attributes, links and malformed entries would change the extracted tree: capture the source snapshot.
then: Each extracted file matches the raw Git object, and each link, special file and attribute-changed input is refused.
notes: Proved by TestSourceArchiveMustMatchRawGitObjects once its name or a subtest carries this ID. TestGitExportAttributesCannotChangeSelectedSource and TestSourceTreeRejectsLinksAndMalformedEntries in the same file cover the refusals.

title: Image verification is exact
when: With an image whose hashes are rebuilt to be consistent after one change: it runs as root, has an ambient environment value, a writable executable, a symbolic link, an extra executable, a private key in its trust store, a device, another owner, or unknown PAX metadata; verify it.
then: Each variant is refused and named.
notes: TestImageRejectsChangedLayoutAndRecord in the same file covers an extra layout file, a link, changed bytes and a missing blob. An excessive size is refused by the layer limit, which no test exercises.

title: Registry transport is bounded and fails closed
when: With a registry that answers over plain HTTP, demands a token from an unapproved origin, redirects with a query string or sends an oversized response: publish and retrieve.
then: Each case fails closed before any credential leaves, and the error names no credential.
notes: TestRegistryTLSCredentialsAndPolicyFailClosed carries this ID. TestRegistryBearerRealmNeedsExplicitApproval, TestRegistryTokenScopeCannotExpandCredentials, TestRegistryResponseAndRequestBounds and TestRegistryBoundaryRejectsCredentialLeaksAndPathEscapes in the same file cover the token origins, the bounds and the errors.

title: A build starts in new folders outside the source, and a failed save leaves no result
when: With a source, a module cache and a folder an interrupted build left: a build is prepared with new folders, then with the interrupted folder as its work or result folder, and with a work or result folder inside the source or a result folder inside the work folder; then the result is saved without an executable and with an executable that differs from the record.
then: Only the new folders are accepted; the source and the interrupted folder keep their files; each failed save removes the result folder it made.
notes: This proves Build's part (appbuild.prepare and appbuild.saveResult in build.go). The image build's part is in internal/appbuild/image.go, which keeps a partial output folder when it fails; the SDK preparation's part is test_existing_output_is_never_removed_or_replaced in scripts/test_compiler_toolchain.py.

title: A declaration without exactly one archetype is refused
when: Checking reads a declaration with no archetype; with two archetypes, test-arch and other-arch, given as a list; with the archetype nonexistent-arch, which the registry does not hold; and with the one archetype test-arch.
then: Expects the first three declarations to be refused with an archetype fault: the first names the archetype as missing, the second names both archetypes, and the third names nonexistent-arch. Expects the last declaration to be accepted.
notes: Proved by TestValidate_MissingArchetype, subtest ST-DECL-INV01-T: no archetype, two archetypes and an unknown archetype are each refused with a fault that names the archetype field (and both names, or the unknown name); one archetype is accepted.

title: A declaration that carries an undeclared field is refused
when: With a declaration that carries a misspelled field at the root, in an entity field, in a collection or in a slot binding: parse it.
then: The parser refuses the declaration with an error that names the unknown field, the file and the line.

title: A declaration must be one document with no anchors, aliases or merge keys
when: With a declaration that holds a second document, an empty second document, an anchor or a merge key: parse it.
then: The parser refuses the declaration with an error that names the fault, the file and the line.

title: A declaration beyond 4 MiB or 128 levels is refused
when: Decode a declaration one byte over 4 MiB, decode a declaration nested 130 levels deep, and parse a file one byte over 4 MiB.
then: Each is refused, and the errors name the nesting limit and the byte limit.

title: A repeated entity name is refused
when: With a declaration that defines the same entity name twice: validate it.
then: The check reports an entity fault that says the entity is defined more than once.

title: A repeated field name in one entity is refused
when: With a declaration whose entity has two fields with the same name: validate it.
then: The check reports a field fault that names the entity and the repeated field name.

title: A field's constraints must suit its type
when: With a declaration whose fields carry constraints that do not suit their types, such as a length limit on a number, a numeric bound on a string, a pattern on a boolean, enum values on a string and a reference target on a string: validate it.
then: The check reports one field fault for each unsuitable constraint, and each fault names the constraint and the field type.

title: A repeated collection name is refused
when: With a declaration that defines the same collection name twice: validate it.
then: The check refuses the declaration with an error that names the repeated name widgets and the line of its second definition (service.yaml:16).
notes: Collections are a map in the declaration format, so a repeated collection name is a repeated key and the declaration cannot be read as one document. ST-DECL-UC04-R06 then holds: the refusal is the one reading fault. This is not the stop at the first fault that ST-DECL-UC03-R02 forbids, so the test does not assert that validation stops.

title: A collection that names an undeclared entity is refused
when: With a declaration whose collection names an entity the declaration does not define: validate it.
then: The check reports a collection fault that names the missing entity.

title: A binding to an undeclared slot is refused
when: With a declaration that binds a policy fill to a slot no component declares: validate it.
then: The check reports a slot fault that names the unknown slot.

title: A binding to a slot no generator invokes is refused
when: With a registry component that declares a slot no registered generator consumes, and a declaration that binds a fill to that slot: validate it.
then: The check reports a slot fault that says no resolved generator consumes the slot.

title: A setting must match its component schema
when: Check setting values against component schema fields of each kind: string, boolean, integer, number, enum, optional, list of strings and list of objects, with both correct and wrong values.
then: Each correct value passes, and each wrong value gets an error that names the type mismatch, the unknown choice, the null, the wrong list item or the unknown or missing nested key.

title: A field default that does not suit the field's type is refused
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD02 with one change each: done (bool) gets the default "yes"; title (string) gets the default 12; a new int field count gets the default 1.5; a new enum field state with the values open and closed gets the default archived. Then it reads TD02 with done given the default true and a new int field count given the default 0.
then: Expects one field fault for each of the first four declarations, each naming the entity, the field, the default and the declared type. Expects no fault for the last declaration.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The test calls checking in process on the declaration as a value, so it needs no stego binary. Each case is its own subtest, with this ID in its name.

title: A component that is not ga is refused unless the declaration accepts it by name, with a reason and a date
when: With the clock set to 2099-01-01, checking reads ST-DECL-TD02 changed to use the alpha component rh-sso-auth of ST-DECL-TD01: with no acceptance; with an acceptance of another component name; with an acceptance of rh-sso-auth with no reason; with an acceptance of rh-sso-auth with no date; and with an acceptance of rh-sso-auth with a reason and the date 2099-06-01. Then it reads the case with no acceptance against a copy of the TD01 registry that puts rh-sso-auth at stage beta. Then it reads TD02 unchanged, which uses only ga components and holds no acceptance.
then: Expects each of the first four declarations, and the case at stage beta, to be refused with a fault that names rh-sso-auth and what the acceptance lacks. Expects the fifth declaration and TD02 unchanged to be accepted.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The clock is an input of checking; the test sets it and does not read the system time. The beta case shows that the rule holds for each stage that is not ga, not only for alpha.

title: An acceptance dated later than its component's sunset is refused
when: With rh-sso-auth at the sunset 2099-12-31 and the clock set to 2099-01-01, checking reads three declarations that accept rh-sso-auth with a reason, until 2100-01-01, until 2099-12-31 and until 2099-12-30.
then: Expects the acceptance until 2100-01-01 to be refused with a fault that names the component, the acceptance date and the sunset date. Expects the other two to be accepted.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The equal date shows that the limit is not later than, not earlier than.

title: A declaration is refused after the date of an acceptance it holds
when: Checking reads a declaration that accepts rh-sso-auth with a reason until 2099-06-01, with the clock set to 2099-05-31 and then to 2099-06-02.
then: Expects the declaration to be accepted at 2099-05-31, and to be refused at 2099-06-02 with a fault that names the component and the date 2099-06-01.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The test sets the clock and does not read the system time. Whether the acceptance holds on 2099-06-01 itself, and in which time zone, waits on ST-DECL-Q04, so the test leaves that day out.

title: The output folder and each factory package are import paths outside the output
when: With an output folder that is not an import path, then a factory package inside the output folder: validate.
then: Each is refused before rendering.
notes: Proved by TestOutputDirectoryMustBeAGoImportPath once its name or a subtest carries this ID. TestApplicationFactoriesRequireGoImportPaths in the same file and TestApplicationFactoryPackagesStayOutsideOutput in preflight_test.go cover the factory rules.

title: Omitted tenancy and audit get their defaults, and a default left with no reason is refused
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD02, which says nothing of tenancy or audit. Then it reads TD02 with tenancy kind single and no reason; with audit off and no reason; with tenancy kind single and the reason Internal tool for one organisation; and with audit off and the reason Stateless proxy with no data of its own.
then: Expects TD02 to be accepted, and the settings that checking gives back to hold tenancy kind pooled and audit level change. Expects the second and third declarations to be refused, each with a fault that names the setting and that a reason is required. Expects the last two to be accepted.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The test calls checking in process on the declaration as a value, so it needs no stego binary. Each case is its own subtest, with this ID in its name.

title: A tenancy claim that is not a path in the verified identity token is refused
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD02 with tenancy kind pooled and the claim org.id; then with a claim that names the request header X-Tenant-ID; then with a claim that names the body field org_id.
then: Expects the claim org.id to be accepted. Expects the header claim and the body field claim each to be refused with a fault that names the claim.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The declaration format (ST-DECL-EN09) does not say how a claim names a request header or a body field, so the two refused cases cannot be written yet. This waits on the Product owner (decisions-for-owner.md, Found in review). A builder must not pass these cases by construction.

title: A controller without tenants each, a collection over a system entity and a tenant binding that writes a shared entity are refused
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD02 with one change each: a controller provisioner with sources scan and watch, resync 10m, replicas 2, lease TTL 15s and tenants none; a new entity Region with tenant system and a collection regions over it; a new entity Plan with tenant shared, a collection plans over it with create, and a binding on plans at before_create that runs as tenant. Then it reads TD02 with the same controller given tenants each, and with the plans binding set to run as system.
then: Expects the first three declarations to be refused, with faults that name the controller provisioner, the collection regions with the entity Region, and the binding on plans. Expects the last two to be accepted.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The controller is complete in each other field, so its one fault is tenants none and not a field that ST-DECL-INV29 asks for. The test calls checking in process on the declaration as a value, so it needs no stego binary. Each case is its own subtest, with this ID in its name.

title: An unknown audit level, sink or sensitivity, and audit annotations that are not a string map, are refused
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD02 with one change each: audit level verbose; an audit sink that is no port binding of the declaration; the sensitivity confidential on the field title; audit annotations on a binding given as a list; and audit annotations with a number value. Then it reads TD02 with audit level metadata, the sink audit-sink bound as a port, the sensitivity pii on title, and the annotations reason=over-limit.
then: Expects each of the first five declarations to be refused with a fault that names the value found, and, for the level and the sensitivity, the allowed set. Expects the last declaration to be accepted.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The test calls checking in process on the declaration as a value, so it needs no stego binary. Each case is its own subtest, with this ID in its name.

title: A schema that does not compile, and a name the schema lacks, are refused
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD03 with one change each: a syntax error on line 4 of authz/schema.zed; the resource type archive on Todo; the permission destroy for delete; the relationship relation approver; and the context field request.region, which no caveat has as a parameter. Then it reads TD03 unchanged.
then: Expects the first declaration to be refused with a schema fault that names authz/schema.zed and line 4. Expects each of the next four to be refused with a fault that names the missing name, its kind and its place in the declaration. Expects TD03 unchanged to be accepted.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not compile a schema yet. The test compiles the fixture schema in process with the compiler that the provider's port names.

title: A slot binding that may write a relation the schema lacks, or one of a type no entity uses, is refused
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD03 with a binding on todos at after_create whose Relationships written is document#viewer; then document#approver; then folder#viewer.
then: Expects document#viewer to be accepted. Expects document#approver to be refused as a relation the schema lacks, and folder#viewer as a resource type no entity of the service declares, each with a fault that names the binding and the relation.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The test calls checking in process on the declaration as a value, so it needs no stego binary. Each case is its own subtest, with this ID in its name.

title: A slot binding or a component setting that holds a bypass flag is refused
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD03 with a binding on todos at before_create that holds a flag that turns the authorization decision off (skip_authz: true); then TD03 with a component setting of the authorization component that does the same; then TD03 unchanged.
then: Expects the first two declarations to be refused, each with a fault of the no-bypass rule (ST-DECL-INV24) that names the binding or the setting. An undeclared-field fault (ST-DECL-INV02) or an undeclared-setting fault (ST-DECL-INV12) alone does not pass. Expects TD03 unchanged to be accepted.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. A flag that no schema declares is already refused as undeclared, so a naive test passes with no bypass rule at all; the test checks the rule that the fault names. What makes a flag a bypass flag is not defined yet (decisions-for-owner.md, Found in review). The clause on the system principal waits on ST-DECL-Q03, so this test leaves it out.

title: Idempotency required on read, list or delete, or not on create, is refused
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD02 with idempotency required on: create; create and patch; patch only; create and read; create and list; create and delete.
then: Expects create, and create with patch, to be accepted. Expects patch only to be refused with a fault that says create is required. Expects each of the last three to be refused with a fault that names read, list or delete.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. Whether update may be named waits on ST-DECL-Q01, so the test leaves update and custom operations out.

title: A float money field, a currency that is not ISO 4217, two currencies in a ledger and an account with no normal balance of debit or credit are refused
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD04 with one change each: a money field price typed as a float; a money field price in integer minor units with the currency EURO; the ledger currency EURO; the ledger currencies EUR and USD; the account customer_wallet with no normal balance; and the account settlement with the normal balance both. Then it reads TD04 with a money field price as integer minor units in EUR.
then: Expects each of the first six declarations to be refused, with a fault that names the field, the currency or the account. Expects the last declaration to be accepted.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The EURO case on the money field shows that the currency rule holds for a money field, not only for the ledger. The test calls checking in process on the declaration as a value, so it needs no stego binary. Each case is its own subtest, with this ID in its name.

title: A ledger collection with update or delete and a stored balance a slot can update are refused, and a pending transfer does not change
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD04 with update added to the transfers collection; with delete added; and with a stored balance field on the accounts and a binding at before_update on their collection. Then the service generated from TD04 runs on a real PostgreSQL: it pends a transfer of 1000 minor units, gets a PUT and then a PATCH to that transfer's path with the amount 2000, then voids the transfer and pends a new transfer of 2000.
then: Expects each of the three declarations to be refused, with a fault that names the collection and the operation, or the binding and the balance field. Expects the PUT and the PATCH each to get a status that is not 2xx, and the stored transfer to keep 1000 and stay pending. Expects the void and the new pending transfer of 2000 to succeed.
notes: Not automated yet: checking and the ledger code are not built. Integration level, because the pending transfer is seen only in the store. The declaration format does not yet say how a stored balance field and a collection over the accounts are written (decisions-for-owner.md, Found in review). The clause on a transfer with one entry waits on ST-DECL-Q02, so this test leaves it out.

title: An unknown mode and kafka-events without durable-events are refused, and event-publisher is accepted with a warning
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD02 with the modes api and worker; with no modes; with the modes api and batch; with the mixin kafka-events alone; with kafka-events and durable-events; and with the mixin event-publisher.
then: Expects api with worker to be accepted. Expects no modes to be accepted with the modes api, worker and controller. Expects batch to be refused with a fault that names batch and the allowed modes. Expects kafka-events alone to be refused with a fault that names durable-events. Expects kafka-events with durable-events to be accepted. Expects event-publisher to be accepted with a warning that names event-publisher as a deprecated alias.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. What event-publisher resolves to is not asserted: ST-DECL-EN01 says durable-events, and ST-SUP-INV17 says durable-events and kafka-events (decisions-for-owner.md, Found in review). The test calls checking in process on the declaration as a value, so it needs no stego binary. Each case is its own subtest, with this ID in its name.

title: A controller with no lease TTL, sources, resync or replicas, or an unknown source, is refused, and a controller runs under a fenced lease
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD02 with a controller provisioner (sources scan and watch, resync 10m, replicas 2, lease TTL 15s, tenants each), then with no lease TTL, with no sources, with no resync, with no replicas, and with the source poll. Then two instances of the controller generated from the first declaration, with the lease TTL 2s, run on one real PostgreSQL. The test stops the instance that holds the lease, then sends a store write with the old fencing token.
then: Expects the first declaration to be accepted and each of the other five to be refused with a fault that names the controller and the field. Expects only the instance that holds the lease to reconcile. Expects the other instance to take the lease only after the stopped holder's lease TTL ends, with a higher fencing token, and the write with the old token to be refused.
notes: Not automated yet: checking and the controller code are not built. Integration level, because the lease and its token are seen only in the store. The statement gives no time limit for the take-over; the test stops waiting after ten lease TTLs only so that it ends, and does not hold the code to a shorter time.

title: A declared invariant of an unknown kind, or without the fields its kind needs, is refused
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD02 with one declared invariant each: unique on Todo by title; no_overlap on Todo with a range and by; sum_limit on Todo with a parent; the kind exclusive; unique with no by; no_overlap with no range; and sum_limit with no parent. Then it reads TD02 with the rule of the kind exclusive written as a binding on todos at before_create instead.
then: Expects the first three to be accepted. Expects each of the next four to be refused with a fault that names the invariant, and the kind or the missing field. Expects the binding to be accepted.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The test calls checking in process on the declaration as a value, so it needs no stego binary. Each case is its own subtest, with this ID in its name.

title: With authorization bound, an entity with no resource type and an operation with no permission are refused, each named
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD03 with one change each: Todo with no resource type; a second entity Tag with no resource type, read by a new collection tags with read, while Todo keeps its resource type; Todo with no permission for list; Todo with no permission for update and none for delete; and list declared public with no reason. Then it reads TD03 with list declared public with the reason the catalog is public by design, and TD02, which binds no authorization and gives Todo no resource type.
then: Expects each of the first five declarations to be refused. Expects the faults to name Todo; Tag; todos and list; todos with update and todos with delete as two faults; and the public list operation with no reason. Expects the last two declarations to be accepted.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The Tag case shows that each entity a collection reads is checked, not only the first. The test calls checking in process on the declaration as a value, so it needs no stego binary. Each case is its own subtest, with this ID in its name.

title: A base path that is not empty or literal and absolute is refused
when: Checking reads one declaration for each base path: empty, /api/v1, api/v1, /, /api//v1, /api/.., /api/%2e and /api/{id}.
then: Checking accepts the empty base path and /api/v1, and refuses each other base path with a base_path error.
notes: Not proof yet: the validate tests check a base path with no leading slash and a valid one, but no test name carries this ID, and no test covers the root, an empty, a dot or an encoded segment. Proof needs one test, with this ID in its name, for each case.

title: A unique-when-live field without one complete unique key is refused
when: Checking reads declarations with a unique-when-live field that is unique, in a composite key with each member live, with no key, with a member that is not live, with the field not in its key, with members in another order, computed, and in an upsert key.
then: Checking accepts the first two and refuses each other declaration with its reason.
notes: Not proof yet: TestValidateLiveUnique covers these cases, but its name does not carry this ID, and no case combines unique with a composite key. Proof needs that case and the ID in the test name.

title: Resource version metadata on an entity that is not versioned, or malformed, is refused
when: ValidateVersioned reads entities that declare generation fields, observations, conditions and cleanup owners without versioned; repeated or badly named owners and conditions; an observation field that is required, has a default or is an upsert key; and a versioned entity with a field named resource_version.
then: ValidateVersioned refuses each with its reason, and accepts a versioned entity with well-formed metadata.
notes: Not proof yet: the tests in versioned_test.go cover observations, cleanup owners and targets and reserved cleanup names, but no test name carries this ID, and no test covers conditions over their limits or a generation field that is computed. Proof needs those cases and the ID in the test names.

title: An installation refuses an existing result folder and keeps what it holds
when: With a result folder that already holds a file: Installation runs into that folder.
then: Installation fails, the file keeps its content, and no download starts.

title: A changed asset or a failed signature leaves no installation
when: With a published release: One asset's bytes change, or a signature check fails, and installation runs.
then: Installation fails, and no result folder and no temporary download remain.

title: A compiler artifact exists only when two isolated builds agree
when: Build the compiler twice from one commit in isolated trees, then compare.
then: The artifact is saved only when both agree; a planted difference saves nothing.
notes: No test yet. CI only today (.github/workflows/compiler-artifact.yml); scripts/test_compiler_artifact.py covers the source inventory half.

title: A release is one immutable tag per commit with four assets
when: Qualify a release whose tag points at another commit, or that holds a different asset set.
then: Qualification fails and names the mismatch.
notes: No test yet. The qualification tests check the tag, the commit and the asset digests; immutability and the burned-tag rule are enforced by the release workflow only.

title: Only the main-branch signing job signs, and only the bytes it fetched
when: Run the artifact workflow from a pull request, from a branch other than main, and by dispatch on main.
then: The pull request and the branch publish no signature; the dispatch on main signs, as a push does; a signing job whose fetched digests differ from the build's signs nothing.
notes: No test yet. Workflow rules only today; no test runs the workflow's job graph.

title: The platform requirements state each need of the components, with its kind and shape, also when two needs have one kind
when: With the declaration and the registry of the test data set, whose components state one need of each of the nine kinds: Write the platform requirements runs; then it runs again with a second secret, payments-api-key with the key token, added to the needs of the SSO JWT verifier; then it runs again with one need taken out of one component's statement.
then: Expects each stated need to be in the written requirements, with its kind, its name, its shape (the keys url and password of the secret orders-database, the port 443 of the egress destination payments) and the component that needs it. Expects the second run to state both secrets, orders-database and payments-api-key with the key token. After the last change, expects the requirement of the need taken out to be gone and each other requirement to be the same.
notes: The data set has one need of each kind, so the second secret is the case that catches a derivation that keeps one need per kind. That the requirements hold no need that the components do not state is ST-DLV-DS01, which ST-DLV-DS01-T02 proves; this test does not assert it.

title: A need that holds an environment value is refused, and the requirements hold no such value
when: With the declaration of the test data set: Write the platform requirements runs once as it is; then once for each of four changes to one component's need, in which the need holds the secret value s3cr3t-password for the key password of the secret orders-database, the host name db.prod.example.com, the address 10.0.0.5, or the namespace orders-prod.
then: Expects the first run to write requirements whose entries hold only a kind, a name, a shape and the component that needs it. Expects each changed run to be refused with a reason that names the component, the need and the field that holds the value, and to give no requirements.
notes: The four values are one of each sort that the invariant names; the check of the written file is a check of its fields, not a search for known values, so that a value of a new sort is also caught.

title: The CI file holds only the pinned call to the shared pipeline and to the STEGO checks
when: With the declaration and the registry of the test data set: Write the delivery pipeline runs for the hosted CI provider, then for Konflux; then both run again with a registry whose pins differ.
then: Expects the hosted CI file to hold one job that calls the shared pipeline by its location at the 40-character commit, and the STEGO checks by their pinned reference, with no step, script or job of its own. Expects the Konflux PipelineRun to reference the standard pipeline bundle and the STEGO checks bundle each by a sha256 digest, with no inline task or script. Expects each file from the second registry to differ from the first only in the lines that hold a pin.

title: The pins and the trusted signer of the CI file are the ones the registry's ci-pipeline component names
when: With the registry of the test data set: Write the delivery pipeline runs for each provider; then the ci-pipeline component is changed to name other pins and another trusted signer, and it runs again.
then: Expects each pinned reference and the trusted signer in each CI file to equal, byte for byte, what the ci-pipeline component names at that run. Expects each CI file to hold no pinned reference and no signer that the ci-pipeline component of that run does not name: after the change, no value of the first ci-pipeline component is left in either file.

title: A candidate from either provider passes only when each of the five STEGO checks passed
when: With a candidate built by the hosted CI provider and one built by Konflux, and fakes of the five checks: Check a delivery candidate runs for each candidate with each check passing; then once for each check, with that one check failing; then once with the result of the executable match missing.
then: Expects both candidates to pass, and Delivery candidate passed to be raised once for each, when all five checks pass. Expects each other run to refuse the candidate, for both providers, naming the check that failed or that did not run, and to raise no Delivery candidate passed.
notes: The checks are drift, vet, test, the reproducible build and the executable match. The missing result is the case that catches a check left out of a provider's list.

title: A candidate passes only when its executable is byte-identical to the one its build record names, from either provider
when: With the build record and the two images of the test data set: the executable match runs on each image; then on a copy of the hosted image and on a copy of the Konflux image, in each of which one byte of the executable is changed.
then: Expects both images to pass, the Konflux image included, since buildah built it from the generated Containerfile. Expects each changed copy to be refused with a reason that names the digest the record names and the digest found in the image.
notes: The changed copy of the Konflux image is the case that catches a match that runs for one provider only, or that trusts the Konflux build in place of the executable.

title: The generated Containerfile builds with the network off, on scratch, to the executable the reproducible build makes
when: With the service of the test data set after stego apply, and its modules prefetched into the build context in the layout that Konflux's prefetch writes: buildah builds the generated Containerfile with the network off; then again with one prefetched module changed so that it does not match go.sum; then again with no prefetched modules.
then: Expects the first build to succeed, its final stage to be FROM scratch, its builder image to be the archetype's Go SDK named by digest, and the sha256 of its executable to equal the executable digest in the build record of stego build for the same revision. Expects the second build to fail naming the module whose checksum differs, and the third to fail without a network fetch.
notes: Runs in CI or in the jshell test namespace, not on the developer workstation. A build that downloads a module must fail the test: the build runs in a network namespace with no route out.

title: The Kubernetes base holds only what the declaration derives, with probes and default resources, and no environment value
when: With the declaration of the test data set, which has an ingress, an egress destination and a secret: Write the Kubernetes base runs; then it runs again with another working folder, other environment variables and an environment file for another environment beside the project; then it runs with the egress destination payments taken out of the declaration.
then: Expects the second run to give the same bytes as the first, so that no resource takes a value from outside the declaration. Expects the third run to differ from the first only in what refers to payments, so that each resource follows an element of the declaration. Expects each container to have the liveness and readiness probes that health-check derives, at its path and port, and the default CPU, memory and ephemeral storage requests and limits. Expects no resource to set replicas, no PodDisruptionBudget, no metadata namespace, no image named by digest, no host name, no egress address or address range, and no Secret data or string data.
notes: Check each resource of the built output, not only the files that STEGO writes today, so that a new resource is also checked. The invariant forbids an image digest; it does not forbid an image name or tag, so the test does not refuse one.

title: The Kubernetes base builds with plain kustomize and no plugin
when: With the service of the test data set after stego apply: the pinned kustomize version builds the base with the network off and with no plugin or exec option; then it builds an overlay fixture that sets the namespace, the replicas and the image digest on the base.
then: Expects both builds to exit 0. Expects the kustomization file to list only files in the base folder, with no remote base, no path out of the folder, no generator or transformer that names a plugin, and no Helm chart.

title: The delivery object takes its cluster, namespace and overlay from the environment files, never from the declaration
when: With the declaration of the test data set: Write the delivery object runs; then it runs with a delivery stanza that also names a destination cluster, a namespace and an overlay path.
then: Expects an ApplicationSet whose template names the service orders, the project orders and the base path, whose files generator lists the platform's environment files, and whose destination cluster, namespace and overlay path are each a parameter of that generator, with no literal value. Expects the second run to be refused, naming the path of each of the three fields in the stanza, and to give no delivery object.

title: A fill manifest that does not name exactly one known slot and one declared collection is refused, naming the field
when: With the built-in registry as the active registry and a declaration with the collection org-users only: the fill manifest reader reads seven fill.yaml files. The first names rest-api.before_create and org-users. The second has no implements field. The third has implements as a list of rest-api.before_create and rest-api.before_delete. The fourth names rest-api.no_such_slot. The fifth names no-such-component.before_create. The sixth names rest-api.before_create and the collection org-groups. The seventh names rest-api.before_create and has no collection field.
then: Expects the reader to accept the first and to give its fill value. Expects it to refuse each of the other six with a fault that names the fill and the field: implements for the second to the fifth, with the value it names for the fourth and the fifth; collection with org-groups for the sixth; and collection for the seventh. Expects no fill value for a refused manifest.
notes: Not automated yet: the check of the slot and the collection against the registry and the declaration is not built. The fourth case catches a check that finds the component and not its slot; the fifth catches a check of the slot name alone, as runRegistryFills matches today. The registry and the declaration are values in memory.

title: Recorded evidence holds the fill digest and the contract digest of the passing run, and keeps them after a later change
when: With untested-fill: compute its fill digest with fill.Digest and the contract digest of rest-api's before_create.proto, record test evidence for it, then change one line of its policy.go and read its fill.yaml again. Then read a fill.yaml whose evidence has no fill digest, and one whose evidence has no contract digest.
then: Expects the evidence in fill.yaml to hold the two digests computed before the run, each as 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits, and to keep them unchanged after the change to policy.go. Expects the reader to refuse each fill.yaml with a missing digest, naming the missing field.
notes: Not automated yet: no command records evidence (ST-EXT-CMD02-H runs the tests only). Compute the expected digests before the run and change the fill after it: a test that computes them after the run passes with code that computes the digests when it reads the manifest. Needs the Go toolchain to run the fill's test.

title: A sign-off is good only with a signature over the digest of its evidence, and new evidence leaves the old sign-off signing nothing
when: With unsigned-fill and listed-ssh: sign off the fill's evidence with stego fill sign. Make a copy of unsigned-fill whose sign-off names the digest of its evidence but carries a signature that listed-ssh made over another digest, and verify that sign-off. Then, in the first fill, change one line of policy.go, record new evidence, and verify the first sign-off against the new evidence.
then: Expects the first sign-off to hold the digest of the evidence and a signature that ssh-keygen -Y verify accepts over that digest with the public key of listed-ssh. Expects the verification of the copy to fail with the reason that its signature does not cover its evidence, and the copy not to be qualified. Expects the verification of the first sign-off against the new evidence to fail with the reason that it signs other evidence, and the fill not to be qualified.
notes: Not automated yet: fill sign (ST-EXT-CMD03-H) and fill.VerifySignOff are not built. Use the real ssh-keygen; a fake signer cannot show that the signature covers the digest. The copy catches a check that compares the evidence digest field and does not verify the signature over it. Do not expect a refusal to store an old sign-off: the second sentence of the invariant lets an old sign-off stay after new evidence, where it signs nothing.

title: A fill with no test file gets no evidence, and STEGO names it
when: With no-tests-fill and untested-fill: record test evidence for both. Then add a file notes_test.txt to no-tests-fill and record test evidence again.
then: Expects fill.yaml of no-tests-fill to stay byte for byte as it was after each run, and the output of each run to name no-tests-fill with the reason that it has no test file. Expects untested-fill to get evidence in the first run.
notes: Not automated yet: no command records evidence. A test file is a Go file whose name ends in _test.go, as go test reads it. The second run catches a check that looks for the word test in any file name.

title: A fill that imports anything but out/slots, the standard library or a listed fill module gets no evidence, naming the import
when: With a declaration that lists the fill module github.com/google/uuid: record test evidence for six copies of untested-fill, each with one import added to policy.go: fmt; github.com/google/uuid; a package under github.com/google/uuid; github.com/google/uuidx; github.com/lib/pq; and the generated package out/internal/storage of the service.
then: Expects the first three copies to get evidence. Expects each of the last three to get no evidence, with fill.yaml byte for byte as it was, and the output to name the copy and the import path.
notes: Not automated yet: no command checks a fill's imports. Resolve github.com/google/uuid, github.com/google/uuidx and github.com/lib/pq through replace directives to fixture modules, and give the uuid fixture a package under its root, because the real module has none. Then only the import check can refuse a copy. The uuidx case catches a check by string prefix. The case of another slot's contract waits for ST-EXT-Q02, and the imports of test files wait for ST-EXT-Q01.

title: Recovery completes an interrupted apply, and plan and drift refuse until it does
when: With a project with applied output and a new plan: Apply stops at each journal point in turn.
then: Plan and drift refuse while the journal is pending. After recovery the output matches the record and no drift remains.

title: A record whose input manifest disagrees with it is refused
when: With a record with an input manifest: The manifest's declaration digest or registry reference differs from the record's.
then: STEGO refuses the record.

title: Apply refuses a plan whose registry content digest differs from the registry it reads
when: With a plan from a loaded registry: The registry content digest in the plan is replaced and apply runs.
then: Apply fails with a registry error and writes no output.

title: Apply refuses a plan that carries another compiler build
when: With a project applied by the current compiler: The compiler build in the plan is changed and apply runs.
then: Apply fails with a compiler error and leaves the record unchanged.

title: Apply refuses a plan when an input, the record or a generated file changed after planning
when: With a project with applied output and a fresh plan: One of service.yaml, go.mod, go.sum, the record, the config or a generated file changes, and apply runs.
then: Apply refuses the stale plan, and the changed file and the record keep their content.

title: A generator that emits one path twice stops planning
when: With a project whose generator returns the same output path twice: Planning runs.
then: Planning stops with a duplicate path error that names the path, and no plan is made.
notes: Two components cannot claim one path, because overlapping namespaces are refused before generators run. This test covers the remaining case, one generator that returns a path twice. The same check in reconciler.go also covers the slot and assembler files, because they join the list before the check runs.

title: A generator file outside its component namespace stops planning
when: With a component that declares an output namespace, and a generator that returns a file outside it: Planning runs.
then: Planning stops with a namespace error.
notes: TestReconcile_NoNamespaceComponentProducingFilesRejected covers the second clause, a component that generates files with no namespace, but has no ID of its own; the one test record names the first case.

title: A plan that writes, deletes or records a path outside the output folder is refused before a fill changes
when: With a project with a hand-written fill, and a plan that names ../fills/policy.go as a file to write, to delete or to record: Apply runs the plan.
then: Apply refuses the plan, the fill keeps its content, and the output folder is not created.
notes: TestApplyRejectsReservedOutputRoots shows the other half: an output folder set to fills, .stego, go.mod or service.yaml is refused.

title: A failed validation, generator or assembly leaves the output and the record unchanged
when: With a project with applied output and a record: A run fails in validation (a missing generator), in a generator (it returns an error) or in the assembler (a circular constructor dependency).
then: The run returns that error, and every file in the project keeps its content.
notes: No saved plan exists yet, so the test cannot show that a failed run saves no plan.

title: The emitted failure record never formats its cause
when: Reports a stage failure whose cause panics when formatted, and the bare cause, into a buffer.
then: Expects the cause kept for errors.Is and errors.As, a five-field record with the fixed event, severity and message, the right stage, and an RFC 3339 timestamp.
notes: Proved by TestFailureRecordDoesNotFormatCause; its name or a subtest must carry this ID. Partial: the stage-name set and the bounded write are asserted by TestFailureOutputHasDeadline and TestFailureOutputDoesNotRetry in the same file.

title: The emitted supervisor waits for a canceled task
when: Cancels a running task that holds its return, then releases it; also starts the supervisor with an already canceled context.
then: Expects no return before the release, a nil result after it, and no task started after cancellation.
notes: Proved by TestCancellationWaits; its name or a subtest must carry this ID. Partial: signal handling and shutdown classification are asserted by TestTaskSignal, TestParentCancellationBeforeChildPropagation and TestCancellationKeepsOtherErrors in the same file.

title: The emitted supervisor contains every kind of task abort
when: Runs a broken task that panics with a string, with nil, with an error whose formatter panics, in a deferred call, or calls Goexit, beside a peer that holds its return; the generated project runs this once more under GODEBUG=panicnil=1.
then: Expects the peer canceled only after the broken task's defers ran, no return before the peer's release, a failure without private text, and the broken task listed once as failed and once as aborted.
notes: Proved by TestAbnormalTaskExitStopsAndJoinsPeers; its name or a subtest must carry this ID. Partial: sorted names and hidden causes are asserted by TestTaskFailureNamesExcludeCauses in the same file.

title: The assembler checks task indexes and keeps task dependencies
when: Assembles with task indexes -1, 1 and 0,0, and computes the consumed constructors for a worker that depends on a store.
then: Expects each bad index refused and the worker's dependency chain consumed.
notes: Proved by TestBackgroundTaskIndexes once its name or a subtest carries this ID. Constructor resources are asserted by TestResourceArgumentsUseTheSelectedDatabase and TestInvalidConstructorResourcesFailAssembly in internal/compiler/resources_test.go; the index and middleware rules by TestConstructorMetadataIndexesMustExist and TestPrimaryMiddlewareSelectionMustBeUnambiguous in internal/compiler/constructor_metadata_test.go.

title: Every component's input check finishes before any component renders
when: With two components where the second refuses the declaration: run apply.
then: The first component renders nothing, and the run stops with the second's refusal.
notes: Proved by TestAllComponentChecksRunBeforeAnyRendering once its name or a subtest carries this ID. Known gap: wiring checks still run after rendering today (compiler-preflight-gap.md), so this invariant is partly false until they move.

title: A constructor dependency names exactly one producer
when: With two components that derive the same value name and a third that depends on it: assemble.
then: Assembly refuses and names the consumer, the dependency and both producers sorted.
notes: Proved by TestAssembleRejectsAmbiguousConstructorDependencies once its name or a subtest carries this ID.

title: The build target meets every active component's minimum Go version
when: With a component whose minimum is above the project's Go target: run apply.
then: Generation stops before any generator runs and names the component and both versions.
notes: Proved by TestGeneratorGoVersionGatesGeneration once its name or a subtest carries this ID. TestPinnedDependenciesGateGoTarget in internal/compiler/dependency_target_test.go covers the dependency-driven minimum.

title: The input manifest is bounded, canonical and digested one way
when: With a manifest that holds 1025 files, an absolute path, a path under the output folder, or a serialised size over 4 MiB: save it.
then: Each is refused and nothing is written; the digest of a fixed manifest matches its vector.
notes: Proved by TestInputManifestRejectsMalformedState once its name or a subtest carries this ID. TestOversizedStateCannotBeSaved and TestInputManifestDigestVector in the same file cover the limit and the codec.

title: A generated symbol never shadows a predeclared or startup name
when: With an import path ending in error and a constructor whose derived name would be NewError: assemble.
then: The import gets a distinct alias used everywhere, and the constructor name is refused before output.
notes: No test yet. Proved by the tests in internal/compiler/symbol_hygiene_test.go and TestAssemble_FillAliasConsistency in assembler_test.go once one carries this ID.

title: A record is upgraded on the next run and decoded strictly
when: With a record that lacks the compiler build, then with one written by a different compiler build, then with one carrying an unknown field: run apply.
then: The first is completed, the second is a record change, the third is refused.
notes: Proved by TestCompilerBuildState once its name or a subtest carries this ID. TestStateFormatRejectsUnsupportedVersions in internal/compiler/state_format_test.go covers strict decoding.

title: Conflicting HTTP routes of two components stop the run
when: ValidateHTTPRouteGroups reads route groups in which two components register the same pattern on the protected multiplexer, a public route conflicts with the protected fallback, and a pattern is not valid.
then: It refuses each group and names the component, and it accepts groups whose protected and public routes do not conflict.
notes: Not proof yet: the tests in http_routes_test.go cover registration failures and the protected mount, but no test name carries this ID. Proof also needs a plan of two components with conflicting routes that writes nothing.

title: Two applies at the same time give one writer and no mixed output
when: Two applies of the same plan start at the same time on one project; then a process that holds the lock dies.
then: Exactly one apply succeeds, the output shows no drift, and the lock is free after the holder dies.
notes: Not proof yet: TestConcurrentApplyHasOneWriter and TestProjectLockIsReleasedWhenProcessDies check this, but their names do not carry this ID. Proof needs the ID in the test names.
